doc.title: Ray Sherman interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998

title: Father Morey Sherman's band and mother's harp-violin duo
summary: His father led a well-known Chicago radio band and his mother played violin in a duo; kids knew his dad.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I understand your parents were musicians?
Yes. That was one of the bands that I listened to on the air, was my dad’s band.

Yeah. Morey Sherman. People from Chicago that remember that period, you know, this is ‘20s and ‘30s would remember him. And my mother also, she worked with a harp and she played violin and she worked with a harpist. They had a harp and violin duo and they played like light classics and things like that. And they were on the air too.
Would they play dinner clubs and stuff like that?
Yeah dinner, a lot of dinner music.
So do you remember, as a kid, you thought your parents were pretty cool because they were out playing gigs?

I guess I was impressed — I mean I took it for granted until kids used to come up and say oh is your father Morey Sherman? Yes. And I said gee I must be special, I didn’t know it was, until that happened. I mean all the music around all the time, that was great. But as far as being special, I didn’t realize it until the kids came up.
That was what they did for a living I guess.

Yeah. And he was very well known around Chicago, my dad. When radio came in he was like on the air three times a day from different places. He’d work like a tea dance and then he’d work a dinner shift, and then he’d go someplace else later at night, all different places. And of course the stations, I guess that was great, they filled up a lot of time with remote broadcasts from the different places. And so he was like a big name in Chicago.
